Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sureshwar Thakur
 Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Sudeepti Sharma

Present: Mr. Sandeep Sharma, Advocate for the petition
 Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl. A.G., Haryana with
 Mr. Saurabh Mago, Dag, Haryana.
 ****
 Sureshwar Thakur, J. (Oral)

1.  In the instant petition, the petitioners pray that a mandamus be issued to the authority concerned,
to release their houses/lands Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners also sought quashing of the impugned order dated 30.11.2017 (Annexure P-9), and, of the notification dated 24.5.2018 (Annexure P-11).

2. The challenge, as made to the annexures (supra), is rested on the premise, that since the petitioners become entitled to a lapsing declaration, thus in terms of Section 24(2) of the Act of 2013, therefore, the launching of the acquisition proceedings through the annexures (supra) be made lapsed.

3. Evidently in the present case, the notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act of 1894'), and, the notification under Section 6 of the Act, became issued respectively in the authenticity of this order/judgement CWP No. 26733 of 2018 -2- 2023:PHHC:159477-DB year 1989, and, in the year 1990, and, they culminated in an award,
becoming rendered in the year 1991.

sentences.text: The purpose of acquisition is for developing Sector-45, Faridabad.
However, for the reasons to be assigned hereinafter, this Court finds no merit in the instant petition.

5. The principal reason for declining the reliefs (supra), as claimed by the writ petitioners, becomes planked on the factum, that the acquiring authority concerned, has adduced cogent discharging evidence, in satisfaction of the duo of parameters, as encapsulated in a verdict rendered by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, inasmuch as, in the signatured synopsis placed today before this Court, does unfold thereins, (i) that the said parameters do become satisfied thus,
through rapat possession No. 66 of 7.10.1991, thus possession of the acquired lands becoming assumed, by the acquiring authority concerned, (ii) that in terms of Section 31 of the Act of 1894, the assessed compensation amount becoming deposited, before the authority concerned, for thereby its becoming released viz-a-viz the land losers concerned.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Since the above adduced discharging evidence is in evident satisfaction of the duo of parameters (supra), as spelt in Indore Development Authority's case (supra), besides when both events (supra)
evidently occurred prior to the coming into force of the Act of 2013.
Therefore, thereby the reliefs (supra), as claimed in the instant petition, thus cannot become assigned to the land losers concerned.

Moreover, when apparently, the acquired lands are required for subserving a public purpose, thereby also this Court does not deem it fit, and, appropriate to scuttle the public purpose,
through assigning reliefs (supra) in favour of the land losers concerned.
authenticity of this order/judgement CWP No. 26733 of 2018 -3- 2023:PHHC:159477-DB 7.
In aftermath, this Court finds no merit in the instant petition, and, the same is hereby dismissed.
8. The pending application(s), if any, is/are also disposed of.
